purpose: Display the existing side-on and elevated Purple Haze studies side by side at equal rendered dimensions, within a separate Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility project, as a quick visual comparison before a proper matched-content gameplay prototype.
scope: One static 1360x800 comparison board containing two original 1024x1024 source concepts scaled independently to 640x640. This is not a playable benchmark, an apples-to-apples camera experiment, a camera decision, final art, or human review.

criteria.visual_source_boundary: These source concepts were made from distinct camera-specific prompts and different seeds. They do not use an identical scene/character identity or identical action pose. Scale and panel rendering are matched; content confounds remain significant.

godot.renderer: GL Compatibility / OpenGL 3.3 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU
godot.runtime_command: godot_console.exe --path <camera-comparison> --scene res://comparison.tscn --audio-driver Dummy --rendering-method gl_compatibility --resolution 1360x800 --fixed-fps 30 --write-movie <absolute camera-comparison-proof.png> --quit-after 1 --log-file <absolute camera-comparison-run.log>

side_on_strengths: Larger, near-camera figures and direct face-to-face staging emphasize character acting, torch silhouette, and cinematic encounter tension.
The violet flame ribbon has a strong large silhouette in open vertical space.
side_on_tradeoffs: The illustration provides little explicit tactical ground-plane/coverage information for the Haze footprint.
It is a single cinematic painting rather than a parallax/route implementation.
elevated_strengths: Ground plane, route, rogue position and smoke-zone occupancy are immediately visible; this supports reasoning about area-control and dodge space.
The frame communicates depth and terrain layout.
elevated_tradeoffs: Hero and rogue are smaller in the 640-square comparable panels; tiny-scale acting/weapon and wind-up are less prominent.
The scene shifts to a different character/pose/landmark arrangement from the side-on source, so this is not an isolated camera variable.
agent_visual_read.current_read: The authored studies illustrate the intended tradeoff: side-on foregrounds silhouette/action presentation; elevated foregrounds tactical space and route/Haze placement. No winner selected.

known_limitations: Different prompts, seeds, character renderings, action/pose, and environment layout confound the camera comparison.
No playable movement, combat, dodge, enemy tell, dynamic effect, animation, collision, camera tracking, or viewport scaling behavior is exercised.
One static generated background image is displayed in each panel; this provides no evidence about browser performance or how a real level would achieve parallax and traversable geometry.
Camera gate remains open pending matched-content playable in-engine tests using the same hero/torch/rogue, attack tell, interaction, Haze zone, route and target viewport.
